This extreme overvaluation is further highlighted by a margin of safety of -865.5% [E34]. Investors are currently paying a premium for future performance that the company is not delivering, with the stock trading at a P/E ratio of 173 [E1]. The market price currently implies an aggressive earnings growth rate of 35.5%, which stands in stark contrast to the 4.0% growth assumed in the base case [E35]. Furthermore, the company offers no dividend yield to compensate for these risks [E4].
